questions.q: What does the Security Console's Simulate Navigator feature actually verify?
options: Which data rows a user can see once a page opens
Function security — which menu and task entries a role or user can reach
The user's password strength
Whether a journal entry balances
questions.explain: Simulate Navigator previews the Navigator menu structure available to a role or user, which confirms function security, not data security.

questions.q: Why can't Simulate Navigator confirm what data a user will actually see?
options: Because it only works for abstract roles
Because Simulate Navigator is only available to Oracle support
Because data security depends on the runtime context of an actual session, which a menu simulation does not create
Because data security doesn't exist in Oracle Fusion
questions.explain: Simulate Navigator is a preview of menu/task access, not a live session, so it cannot evaluate data security policies that depend on real runtime context.

questions.q: What is the appropriate way to verify a user's actual data access before go-live?
options: Use a dedicated test user account provisioned with the identical role and data access, then sign in as that test account
Borrow a real employee's login credentials and sign in as them
Assume the role is correct if it looks right in the Security Console's hierarchy view
Skip verification since Simulate Navigator already covers everything
questions.explain: Because Simulate Navigator can't confirm data visibility, a dedicated test account mirroring the real assignment is the standard, appropriate way to verify actual behavior. Borrowing a real employee's credentials is never appropriate.

questions.q: In the recommended two-step verification workflow, what comes first?
options: Signing in as a test user account
Deleting the role and rebuilding it from scratch
Filing a support ticket with Oracle
Simulating function security with Simulate Navigator
questions.explain: The workflow starts with Simulate Navigator to confirm function security quickly, before moving to a test account for data security verification.

questions.q: On the Simulate Navigator page, what does a padlock icon next to a menu or task entry indicate?
options: The entry is currently authorized and in active use
The entry has been permanently deleted from the system
The entry can be included in a Navigator menu but isn't currently authorized for the selected role or user
The entry requires a password reset
questions.explain: A padlock marks a menu or task entry that could potentially be included but is not currently authorized for the role or user being simulated.
